column1: The FOMC’s December 2018 statement signals a strong current economy (solid job gains, low unemployment, robust household spending) and inflation near its symmetric 2% objective, coupled with a 25 bp rate hike to a 2.25–2.50% target range (IOER at 2.40%) and continued balance-sheet runoff. Interpreted through the literature: (1) With longer-term inflation expectations “little changed,” gradual tightening is consistent with inflation-forecast targeting and adherence to the Taylor principle, which helps anchor inflation around target (Svensson; Woodford). (2) Emphasis on credibility and a symmetric 2% goal addresses the classic inflation-bias problem under discretion (Barro–Gordon), and aligns with Friedman–Phelps’ view that there is no durable unemployment–inflation trade-off. (3) Noting that business fixed investment has moderated accords with macro-finance evidence that higher real rates and tighter financial conditions temper investment and near-term output (Ang–Piazzesi; Rudebusch–Wu; Christiano–Eichenbaum–Evans). Overall tone: positive on current conditions but modestly hawkish for the outlook given “some further gradual increases” in rates and tighter financial conditions. sentiment score = 0.55
